transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. It's very nice to meet you, too. Thank you for taking the time to see me. I, um... I hope I'm not wasting your time or anything. 

It's just... things at the warehouse have been really difficult lately. I drive a truck there, and... gosh, I feel a little embarrassed even saying this out loud. I don't want you to think badly of me, but... the routing system we use, it's—it's not just a computer to me anymore. I know it sounds strange, but I know it's been marking my moves. It sends these messages through the scanners, and I just know it's doing it to push me out, because I'm one of the old hands. 

I hope that makes sense... am I explaining that okay for you?
Aside from the messages on the scanner, have you been hearing any voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear?

Oh, boy... I, um... I really hate to admit this. I don't want you to think I'm crazy, Dr. Smith. I'm a good, reliable worker, I promise. But... well, yes. I guess I have been hearing some things. 

I try to just brush it off as stress, you know? But sometimes, even when I'm just sitting out in my own garage at home, with the truck off and everything completely quiet... I hear the dispatch voices. Just as clear as day. They, um... they call out my operator number. And they say that I'm dangerous, or that security is coming to get me. 

It's probably just my mind playing tricks on me from being around the loud equipment so much, or just being overtired, right? I mean, does that sound like something that happens when a person is just under a whole lot of pressure? I really hope it's okay that I shared that with you, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about the scanner and hearing these dispatch voices?

Well, gosh... I, um... I guess it's been going on for a little while now. I really tried to just ignore it, you know? I figured if I just put my head down and worked harder, it would all sort itself out. 

But if I really think about it, the... the things with the scanner, and hearing the dispatch voices when no one is there... it's been about a year and eight months. I know that probably sounds like a long time to let something like this go, and I'm really sorry if I should have come in sooner. I just didn't want to make a fuss or have anyone think I couldn't handle my job. I'm usually very steady, I promise. Does... does that make sense, why I might have just tried to push through it for that long?
Outside of these experiences, have you noticed any changes in your ability to take care of yourself, such as a loss of interest in your usual hobbies or difficulty keeping up with your daily hygiene?

Oh, um... well, I really try to keep myself presentable, Dr. Smith. I wouldn't want anyone at work to think I'm letting myself go. My hygiene is fine, I make sure of that. I shower and shave, you know, just like always. I hope that's what you were asking? 

But, um... as for hobbies... gosh, I feel a little guilty saying this, like I'm just being lazy or something. But... well, I used to love fishing. And I sang in the choir, and I'd spend hours just tinkering with wood in the garage. Those things used to really settle me down. 

Lately, though... I don't know, it's probably just because I'm getting older and maybe a bit worn out from the warehouse, right? But I can look right at my fishing rods, or my woodworking tools, and... I just feel no pull to touch them at all. I just sit there. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just giving up or anything. Is it normal to just sort of... lose your spark for things when you're under a lot of stress?
When you are speaking with others, do they ever tell you that they have trouble following your train of thought or that your words don't seem to make sense?

Oh, no, sir. I don't... I don't think so. I always try to be very careful with how I speak to people, especially at the warehouse. I wouldn't want anyone getting confused on the floor, you know? Safety first and all that. 

So... no, no one has ever told me my words don't make sense or that they can't follow me. I really hope I'm making sense to you today, Dr. Smith. I try hard to keep my thoughts organized so I can give you the right answers and not waste your time. Am I... am I communicating okay with you so far?
Have you noticed any times where you have felt frozen, unable to move or speak, or perhaps found yourself acting in a way that seemed strange or unusual to others?

Well, um... I really don't want to make it sound like I'm acting crazy or anything, Dr. Smith. I'm usually very reliable, I promise. But... gosh, this is a little embarrassing to admit. 

Sometimes, I guess... well, it happens at work, and even at home a few times. I just get so... mixed up in my head. I'll just sort of freeze up, and I don't even realize I'm doing it at first. People will be trying to talk to me, and I'll just be standing there, holding my hands out in the air like they're still on the forklift controls. And I guess I start repeating this one safety phrase over and over again, without even meaning to. 

I know that must look so strange to the other guys on the floor. I feel awful about it, really. I hope they don't think I'm losing my mind or that I can't do my job safely anymore. It's just a little hiccup, right? I mean, I'm sure it's just from working so hard for so many years... does that sound like something that just happens when you're tired?
